docs.text: The Chicago River has flowed out of, not into, Lake Michigan since 1900.
As big as the Great Lakes are, their watershed is pretty small. With the Chicago River flowing backwards to the Mississippi, Chicago is on the .bsky.social lakefront, but not in the watershed.

The Chicago River is technically not part of the Great Lakes watershed. It actually sucks water out of Lake Michigan and sends it down the Mississippi River. Also how do 844 people die on a docked boat?

The Chicago River used to flow into Lake Michigan, but it was polluted and the city gets their water from the lake so in 1900 they reversed the flow of the river. Now it flows from Lake Michigan into the Mississippi watershed.
The Chicago River doesn’t empty into Lake Michigan. The flow was reversed famously in the early 1900’s and empties into the Mississippi River eventually.
Chicago had historic roots in the interface between the Great Lakes and Mississippi River system, and might not arise again given modern transportation.

River Lake: Both MN and Chicago are defined by rivers (Headwaters of the Mississippi and Chicago famously reversed the flow of the Chicago River to keep industrial waste out of Lake Michigan) and lakes (Land of 10,000 Lakes and Lake Michigan) 1/3
Seriously? Illinois contributes next to nothing to Lake Michigan water levels and because Chicago reversed the flow of the Chicago River, is actually a net drain on water levels.
They changed the Chicago River, and instead of contributing to the watershed, it drains even more water away from the watershed. Chicago is a net drag on the Great Lakes.
Chicago adds nothing to the Great Lakes water basin. In fact they reversed flow on the Chicago River and send Great Lakes water down to the Mississippi River.

I am ok with cities that contribute to the watershed to draw water out. Because their treated waste water will return to the watershed, not get sent down the Mississippi River like Illinois cities do. Illinois and Chicago are a net drag on the Great Lakes. They are takers.
